title: SIGTERM commits and pushes before the container dies
description:
The platform's eviction is graceful and the runway is enormous: SIGTERM to the main process, then 'waits up to 15 minutes for that process to exit', then SIGKILL (https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/platform-details/).

Fifteen minutes is far more than enough to commit and push. Using thirty seconds of it converts most evictions from 'lose a tick' into 'lose nothing'. This is the single most valuable affordance the platform gives this design, and today nothing uses it.

The run keeper already pushes the run branch on a timer, so some of this exists; this tick makes the eviction case explicit and bounded rather than relying on when the timer last fired. Handle SIGTERM: commit what is in the worktrees, push, write the checkpoint, then exit - with a bound so a hung push cannot eat the whole grace window and reach SIGKILL anyway.

Do not use the grace window for anything else. It is for making the disk's loss survivable, not for finishing work.
